newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyocera enjoys record group sales but profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Kyocera enjoys record group sales but profits fall.

text.p: Kyocera Corp announced mixed earnings results on Friday, with annual profits falling but group sales hitting a record high due to soaring demand for its communications equipment.

Kyocera's telecommunication division saw sales soar on the back of booming demand for its cellular phones and personal handyphone systems (PHS). This helped boost group sales to a record 714.77 billion yen in 1996/97, which ended in March.

Domestic sales grew about 13 percent, helped by the robust telecommunications sector, while the yen's weakness against major currencies over the year helped push up overseas sales by eight percent, the ceramics maker said in a statement.
But Kyocera's group net profit fell 45 percent to 45.65 billion yen in 1996/97, reflecting losses at its PHS units. PHS is a low-cost portable phone service.
For the current fiscal year, a company official told reporters that the company would enjoy a 58 percent rise in group net profit to 72 billion yen.

The company said it would try to strengthen production in Asia in an attempt to offer electronics components and ceramic components to the region's fast-growing market. It will also consider expanding production in China, it said.
On a parent basis, Kyocera's current profits rose 3.9 percent to 96.91 billion yen in 1996/97, and it forecast a 9.4 percent profit rise this fiscal year.
